english.proper: Solemn Intercession II: For the Pope
english.problem: 'qui elegit eum in ordine episcopatus' (ablative) is 'chose him in the order of the episcopate', not 'for the order of bishops' (purpose/destination); the 1962 study English of the same clause ([good-friday Solemn Intercessions]) already reads 'in the order of the episcopate'.

(1) Trisagion: 'Sanctus Fortis' / 'Sanctus Immortalis' are substantival vocatives ('Holy Strong One', 'Holy Immortal One'); 'Holy and Strong' / 'Holy and Immortal' insert 'and' and turn the titles into paired adjectives (x3 each). (2) 'et tu me flagellatum tradidisti': perfect participle = 'you handed me over, scourged', not 'to be scourged' (that would be flagellandum).
Without a comma after 'slain' the infinitive can be read as the purpose of the slaying; the Latin sets 'qui occisus est' off with commas.
Same as easter-3-friday Entrance Antiphon: comma needed after 'slain'.
'festinantes' (acc. pl., object of impediant) refers to the same 'nos' as the second clause; 'those hastening' makes it third person and breaks the reference to 'us'.
'ad tam miram huius sancti luminis claritatem': 'tam' (so) is not rendered.

withdrawn_entries.problem: Transcription is exact (Lasance PDF p. 1343, printed 1321, image read), but the English does not render the target Latin in its last clause: 'nomina autem eorum vivent in saeculum saeculi' ('for ever and ever') is given as 'their names shall live unto generation and generation', which is the Douay rendering of the Vulgate Ecclus 44:14 'in generationem et generationem' - a different Latin. Fails the clause-by-clause test of DECISIONS 9d; the antecedent route requires the English to render the identical Latin.
